reuse.why: Keeps using getNextDate and getWeekendAdjustedDay, but does not teach getWeekendAdjustedDay (the existing single weekend-handling helper) about daily frequency, so each caller works the rule out around it.

duplication.why: The 'daily && skipWeekend' predicate is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and (as bare isDaily) in schedule-template, and the weekend filter plus lookahead is re-implemented in getUpcomingDates with a different window (count*2 vs 7).

placement.why: Core logic sits in shared/schedules.ts and frequency is threaded through parseRecurDate, but part of the rule is decided in server/schedules/app.ts and budget/schedule-template.ts.

scope.why: Only the daily-skip rule, its plumbing, null-handling it needs, and tests.

maintainability.why: Three call sites decide 'does this schedule skip weekends' with three different expressions and lookahead sizes, so a later change to the rule must be found and kept consistent in each.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates computes its own skipsDailyWeekend and passes 'skipWeekend && !skipsDailyWeekend' into getWeekendAdjustedDay, filtering weekends itself instead of going through getNextDate's handling.

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates re-expresses getNextDate's take-more/filter-weekends logic as an occurrences(count*2).filter().slice() chain with its own predicate name.

one_place.where: The daily-skip decision is computed independently in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate (skipsDailyWeekend), server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates (skipsDailyWeekend) and budget/schedule-template.ts (isDaily); there is no single shared definition.
